record.paper_title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: If X has a norming Markushevich basis and Z is a complemented subspace of X, must Z admit a norming Markushevich basis?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.12. Let X be a Banach space with norming M-basis and Z be a complemented subspace of X. Must Z admit a norming M-basis?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a (real or complex) Banach space with topological dual X*. A biorthogonal system {(x_i, x_i^*) : i ∈ I} ⊂ X × X* (so x_j^*(x_i) = δ_{ij}) is called a Markushevich basis (M-basis) of X if the linear span of {x_i : i ∈ I} is dense in X and the functionals {x_i^* : i ∈ I} separate the points of X. A closed subspace N ⊆ X* is called norming if the formula |||x||| := sup{|f(x)| : f ∈ N, ||f|| ≤ 1} defines an equivalent norm on X. An M-basis {(x_i, x_i^*)} of X is called norming if the closed linear span in X* of {x_i^* : i ∈ I} is a norming subspace of X*. A closed subspace Z of X is complemented if there exists a bounded linear projection P : X → X with P(X) = Z.

Question: Suppose X is a Banach space that admits a norming M-basis and Z is a complemented subspace of X. Must Z admit a norming M-basis?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether the existence of a norming M-basis passes to complemented subspaces is reported as still open in recent survey/research literature on norming Markushevich bases, in contrast to known facts that existence of M-bases does not pass to all subspaces while shrinking M-bases do.

status_evidence.title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys recent results and lists open problems concerning norming M-bases, including questions about heredity to complemented subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question whether norming M-bases pass to complemented subspaces is listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-greedy Markushevich bases, duality and norming subspaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on Markushevich bases and norming subspaces; does not resolve the complemented-subspace heredity question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research on norming M-bases does not announce a solution to the complemented-subspace problem.
